title: Bramble and Cora's Raindrop Concert
markdown:
Sunrise burst. Bramble the bunny’s nose twitched. His whiskers wiggled. The morning air felt sharp and keen. Outside his cozy burrow, a sunbeam painted warm gold stripes across the dewy green grass. It wasn’t just any morning. Bramble blinked. Today felt special.

A happy chirp zipped past his floppy ear. Cora the cockatiel landed with a gentle flutter on his windowsill, yellow crest bobbing like a tiny sun. “Bramble. Bramble. Wakey, wakey!” she trilled, tinkling bells. “It’s a perfect day.”

Bramble bounced out of his mossy bed. “Perfect for what, Cora?” His fluffy tail gave a little flick.

Cora winked. “A surprise. A secret breakfast concert. For everyone in Sunny Meadow.”

Bramble’s long ears perked. “A concert.” He hopped to the window. Birds were already tweeting. The world woke with a happy buzz. “We’ll need yummy plump berries. And the crunchiest crispest lettuce.”

“And my little painted drum,” Cora puffed her chest. “And your special twig whistle. The one that makes such a cheerful TOOT.”

Bramble nodded, mind buzzing. “Yes. Oh, yes. But… what if it rains?” He pointed a paw. Way at the sky’s edge, a soft grey smudge grew.

Cora’s crest drooped a tiny bit. “Oh dear. Raindrops might be coming. Quick, Bramble, quick. We have to be super speedy.”

And then they dashed. Bramble, THUMP-THUMP-THUMP, bounded toward the juicy berry bush. He gathered plump red globes, skins gleaming. Cora, FLAP-FLAP-FLAP, swooped to the lettuce patch and plucked the greenest leaves.

“Berries here. Big juicy ones,” Bramble called.

“Lettuce there. So crunchy and grand,” Cora chirped, beak full.

They zoomed back to the burrow. The grey smudge was bigger. A low rumble echoed, like a giant yawning.

“Quick, the drum,” Cora nudged her painted drum. “You get the whistle ready.”

Bramble picked up his favourite twig, smooth from many happy tunes. He blew a quick sharp happy note. TOOT!

“Perfect pitch,” Cora giggled, a little hop. She tapped a bouncy rhythm. TAP-TAP-TAP.

The sky rumbled louder. A fat raindrop splatted on Bramble’s twitchy nose. His whiskers trembled. Ears flopped. The concert might be ruined.

“Don’t worry,” Cora’s crest stood tall. “We’re almost there. Just one more thing for our feast.”

She darted inside and popped out with two bright pebbles from the stream. “For our breakfast. Crunchy and yummy to munch on.”

Bramble grabbed a big clean leaf for a plate. Cora arranged berries and lettuce. Just as Bramble was about to blow his first song, a soft PITTER-PATTER began on the leaves. Then another. Then a gentle steady DRUM-DRUM-DRUM of rain.

“It’s here,” Bramble squeaked.

Cora didn’t miss a beat. TAP-TAP-DRUM. “Then let’s make music with it.”

Bramble put the whistle to his lips. He blew a bright cheerful melody that danced with the falling drops. TOOT-TOOT-DANCE. The rain pattered. The whistle soared.

They ate their breakfast concert. Berries popped with sweetness. Lettuce crunched. The rain drummed a soothing beat outside, a natural accompaniment. Bramble and Cora giggled. The surprise was a smashing, splashing success, all before the sun was fully awake.

“Today,” Bramble declared, munching a particularly juicy berry, “is going to be AMAZING!”

Quick, Bramble, quick: another TOOT, another TAP-TAP-TAP, and they kept playing, ready for whatever fun the bright new day would bring.
